content: The dithionate anion, represented as S₂O₆²⁻, is a sulfur oxoanion that originates from dithionic acid (H₂S₂O₆). Its chemical formula is sometimes expressed in a semi-structural format as [O₃S-SO₃]²⁻. The sulfur atoms in the dithionate ion are in the +5 oxidation state, which is attributed to the presence of the sulfur-sulfur (S-S) bond. Dithionates generally form stable compounds that are resistant to oxidation or reduction under normal conditions. However, strong oxidizing agents can oxidize dithionates to sulfates, while strong reducing agents can reduce them to sulfites and dithionites. Aqueous solutions of dithionates are notably stable and can withstand boiling without undergoing decomposition. When crystalline dithionates are exposed to gamma irradiation, SO₃⁻ radical ions are produced. In the hydrated form of dithionates, the molecular structure is staggered, whereas in the anhydrous potassium salt form, the structure is nearly eclipsed.
